Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — clinical summarization workload

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — quick context: EmberMed is standardizing clinical note summarization across our ambulatory suite. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for Q1 2028. Early traffic estimates: ~800k tokens/day with expected peak windows that could reach 250 tokens/sec sustained for ~3 hours during morning batch processing and spikes up to ~1.2k tokens/sec for short bursts (several minutes).

SLO goal: p95 generation latency <= 800ms for the baseline summarization model (we're profiling against a 13B/70B open model family, leaning to 70B quantized for quality).

Can you sketch required reserved capacity (GPUs), recommended headroom multiplier, and what a canary ramp would look like? Also helpful: what baseline tokens/sec numbers you assume per GPU for H100 vs A100 for a 70B quantized model at perf-opt?

Attached is a short workload spec and example payloads (embermed_specs_v0.3.pdf).

Elena Park
Head of Platform
EmberMed

Elena — thanks, this is exactly the right level of detail to start. I took a quick pass and attached a one-page initial assumptions workbook (initial-thoughts.xlsx) that lists the traffic buckets and our first-order GPU mapping. High-level asks from our side:
- Can you confirm typical request length distributions (avg tokens per request, 90th token length)?
- Are you able to run a small sample of requests against a 13B variant to validate prompt sizes?

Preliminary notes:
- If you plan to standardize on a quantized 70B runtime, we typically model at ~1.0–1.4k tokens/sec per H100-equivalent for generation at 512 token contexts with optimized kernels and KV-cache warm. A100 is commonly ~0.6–0.9x that throughput depending on kernel maturity and quantization format.
- To meet p95 < 800ms we model tail latency sensitivity to concurrency more than raw tps — this pushes us to prefer slightly higher reserved slab for predictable p95.

Tagging Kim (solutions) for any product guardrails and Mina (infra) for concrete H100/A100 tps tables. Ben, please pick up procurement/timing questions once we have a target slab size.

Thanks,

Karthik — quick engineering calibration based on our latest perf suite. Copying the brief here and attaching the perf table (gpu_perf_table.csv).

Quoted assumptions from Karthik:
> we typically model at ~1.0–1.4k tokens/sec per H100-equivalent for generation at 512 token contexts with optimized kernels and KV-cache warm. A100 is commonly ~0.6–0.9x that throughput depending on kernel maturity and quantization format.

Our more deterministic numbers (70B quantized, 512 context, batch size tuned for latency):
- H100 (fp8/4-bit quantized path, optimized kernels): 1,250 tokens/sec median, p95 amplification factor ~1.4 => p95 ~1,750 tokens/sec effective for concurrency planning (we model p95 headroom by reducing effective capacity).
- A100 (ampere gen, same quant path): median 780 tps, p95 amplification factor ~1.5 => p95-equivalent ~520 tps effective.

Headroom guidance: for commitments we recommend reserving capacity to cover 95% of expected peak slices after a 1.4x headroom multiplier on p50 throughput (this buys stable p95 behavior without overprovisioning). For your peak burst pattern (1.2k short spike): one H100 should handle short 1.2k spikes (median), but not sustained at p95 targets.

Example sizing math (ballpark):
- Sustained morning window: 250 tps sustained. Using H100 effective p95-equivalent 1,750 tps => a single H100 covers baseline sustained with ~7x buffer. But p95 tail modes during concurrency can reduce effective capacity — we apply the 1.4x headroom for safety.
- If you require strict p95 <= 800ms across spikes and sustained windows, we recommend a commit slab of 4 H100s to give room for concurrent requests + KV-cache warmups + background system tasks. Canary = 1–2 H100s for 2 weeks with traffic mirroring.

If you want an A100-only option for cost-sensitivity, expect to need ~6 A100s for similar p95 headroom (rough order).

Attachment: gpu_perf_table.csv (perf stubs)

Let me know if you want a 2-page capacity plan I can turn into a PDF for the customer-facing deck.

— Mina
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elena — following up with a draft capacity plan based on the spec you shared and Mina's perf calibration. Key bullets (attached as redwood_capacity_plan_v1.pdf):

- Baseline assumptions: 70B quantized model, 512 token output contexts, median tokenization ~85 tokens/request, morning sustained window 250 tps, short spikes to 1.2k tps.
- Recommended committed slab: 4x H100 (reserved). Rationale: each H100 gives ~1,250 median tps; applying 1.4x headroom and p95 sensitivity yields effective p95-equivalent ~900–1,100 tps total slab capacity for concurrency. 4 H100s provide runway for growth and maintain p95 < 800ms in our simulations.
- Canary & rollout: start with a 2-H100 canary (traffic shadowing and 10% traffic mirroring) for 10 business days, collect p95 & token burn metrics, then increase to 4 H100 reserved on a 90-day commit. Auto-fallback policy to smaller quantized variant (13B quant) if we detect sustained p95 degradation or KV-cache coldness.
- A100 alternative: ~6 A100 reserved to match p95 headroom. Tradeoff: lower unit cost but higher ops variability and less graceful p95 tail.
- Ops considerations: KV cache warmup strategy (pre-warms during 15–30m pre-peak), token-level throttling for external API consumers, and prioritized queuing to protect interactive latency.
- Estimated committed monthly cost (order-of-magnitude): provided separately by Ben after he factors in regional pricing and discounts (Ben, can you drop a cost stub?)

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/EMB-2027-019), shared capacity sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdE_embermed-capacity

Attachment: redwood_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (customer-facing summary)

If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with engineering + procurement this week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
